episodes.200639: Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms developed in the warm sector behind a weakening frontal boundary that stretched from eastern Georgia and arced back into northeastern Arkansas.  One of these storms produced up to three quarter of an inch in diameter hail.
episodes.200678: Strong showers and thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the Brevard County coastline.
episodes.201009: Mid level height falls ahead of an approaching trough resulted in the development of scattered convection throughout the day. Given dry low levels and a well mixed boundary layer, DCAPE values were high, and numerous dry to mostly dry microbursts were observed across Utah.
episodes.201076: A variety of weak short-wave troughs moving through southwest flow aloft combined with a slow moving frontal boundary to produced thunderstorms over parts of western and central North Dakota.  The thunderstorms were very short-lived, but were able to produce brief severe wind gusts over southwest North Dakota due to a very dry lower atmosphere. The strongest reported wind gust of 77 mph occurred at the Hettinger Airport in Adams County.
episodes.201347: A trough over the lower Mississippi valley region brought waves of showers and embedded storms across central North Carolina. One storm cell became tornadic over Edgecombe County in the late afternoon hours, producing EF1 tornado damage.
episodes.201510: Slow moving thunderstorms produced isolated areas of flash flooding.
episodes.201565: Severe storms in Flathead and Sanders counties produced hail up to one inch in diameter.
episodes.201803: A high-end EF-1 tornado struck the community of Langley, SC overnight on May 12th. The tornado was embedded within an area of heavy rain in an otherwise unfavorable environment to severe weather across the area. It was the only severe report of the event other than some minor flash flooding that was reported later that morning across northern Orangeburg county.
episodes.202155: Deep layer SW flow was across the local area with passing upper-level energy around a stacked low-pressure system over the southern MS River Valley. Strong to isolated severe storms developed which produced gusty winds.
episodes.202300: A cold front produced afternoon scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms across the region. A thunderstorm produced severe thunderstorm winds along the Hi-line. A strong pressure gradient setting up in Southwest Montana produced isolated strong wind gusts.
episodes.202822: Scattered thunderstorms developed as warm air surged northward in eastern Georgia. A few storms became strong with damaging winds and some hail. Slow moving storms trained over a few locations resulting in heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.202886: A closed low to the southwest of East Tennessee brought marginal amounts of instability and shear to the region. With a pause in the rain, an isolated severe storm was able to form, bringing hail and severe winds to a small portion of the area.
episodes.202988: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms impacted portions of the Atlantic coastal waters and the coastline. These storms developed in the vicinity of a nearby stationary boundary and produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.202989: Clusters of thunderstorms developed in the early morning hours near a stationary boundary associated with an area of low pressure situated near the lower Mississippi Valley. These thunderstorms moved along the coast through the morning producing strong wind gusts.
episodes.203189: Low pressure and an associated cold front moved across Wyoming and brought severe thunderstorms with high wind gusts to much of western and central Wyoming. The strongest wind occurred west of Highway 120 near Irma Lake where a wind gust of 79 mph was measured. Other notable wind gusts included 75 mph along South Pass near Red Canyon, 70 mph at Farson in Sweetwater County, 66 mph at the Dubois airport, and 62 mph in Powell, WY.
episodes.203368: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed across upstate South Carolina during the evening. One storm produced a brief tornado in Abbeville County. Storms and clusters tended to move slowly, resulting in locally heavy rainfall, with isolated flash flooding developing where multiple storms moved over the same areas.
episodes.203451: A strong cold front pushed through the Idaho Panhandle on May 11. Thunderstorms along the front brought hail, strong winds, and heavy rain. Rain amounts were up to a quarter of an inch. High wind gust in the region was 56 MPH near Fraser. Hail size of one inch was reported near Pinehurst.
episodes.203574: A surface front associated with an area of low pressure moving across the southern United States slowly approached Florida from the eastern Gulf. The moist air mass ahead of the front allowed for flooding from excessive rainfall and for strong to severe thunderstorms to develop.
episodes.203716: A weak shortwave produced thunderstorms over the mountains that strengthened near Custer County. Mainly produced strong winds.
episodes.203788: For the second day in a row severe weather was widespread throughout southeast Idaho.

A National Weather Service Storm Survey team confirmed a brief high-end EF-1 tornado with winds up to 105 mph in Langley, SC that occurred around 330 am. The tornado began near Pinecrest Drive snapping several large branches before uprooting numerous trees in Langley Cemetery. Moving northwest, the tornado snapped numerous trees and caused minor roof damage to multiple homes between Piney House Road and Chaffee Street. After crossing near Cushman Road, the tornado caused substantial tree, siding, and shingle damage between Piney Heights Road and Dunbar Street. The fire department and adjacent structures along Augusta Road then sustained high-end EF-1 damage with garage door failure, outbuildings destroyed, and the metal roofing ripped off and thrown several hundred yards. Additional tree damage occurred along Langley Dam Road with dozens of uprooted trees before dissipating near Jefferson Davis Highway.

An EF-1 tornado touched down in the Southern Terrace area of Princeville, NC, during the afternoon hours on Monday May 12, 2025, and traveled north into a farm field in Tarboro. The tornado damaged a farm outbuilding along with several irrigation pivots, snapping several large trees along the way. The tornado then continued north along Wooten Street before dissipating near Elm Street.

Several large trees scattered about were felled by severe thunderstorm winds on private property and seen in southwestern Meigs County, on both sides of the Hiwassee River and near Highway 58 for a few miles north of the river. One of the trees on the private land was snapped, the rest were felled at their roots. At least one road was impassable due to the tree damage.

Severe thunderstorm caused several trees to fall across the county, knocking over powerlines in a few locations. Power outages amounted to 10 percent of the county being without power due to the storm.

A supercell thunderstorm moved northeast across Palm Beach County, generally from Lion Country Safari, through Westlake, and into the Acreage. This storm did not produce a continuous tornado, however, brief EF0 level touchdowns were identified in the damage survey. In general, the majority of the damage was located in the Acreage and was confined to minor tree damage at the low end of the EF0 scale, and damage to outdoor equipment and furniture. There were, however, a couple locations where large pines were snapped near the trunk, resulting in a high end EF0 classification.
